articles.title: How can I get the report? How do you send it to me?
articles.content:
We provide reports in a special section of the Personal Account called "Reports".

We no longer send reports via emails.

articles.title: How frequently do you send reports? When will I receive my first report?
articles.content:
Reports are provided on a semi-annual or quarterly basis, according to the terms specified in the Agreement.

Quarterly reports are sent 45 calendar days after the end of the quarter, i.e. 

May 15 for Q1, August 15 for Q2, November 15 for Q3, and February 15 for Q4 of the previous year.


Please note that compensation for the use of your repertoire under related rights is reflected in the report with a lag of 1 quarter, necessary for processing and checking the report from the platform and receiving the payment. 

For compensation under copyright, the lag may be 1-2 quarters, depending on the specific storefront and its schedules for processing applications and making payments.


For example, if you uploaded your repertoire in Q1, the funds for its use will only be received by us in Q2 and will be reflected in the Q2 report, which will be sent to you in Q3.


The first report will be sent to you within 45 days after the end of the first quarter in which you uploaded your repertoire.

articles.title: What information is included in the report?
articles.content:
The report contains information on the amounts received from platforms for your repertoire during the previous reporting period. You can see the total amount of royalty for the reporting period on the first tab "Summary", and the breakdown of this amount by compositions and phonograms on the other tabs.


There are additional tabs "Compositions" and "Recordings", which show detailed information on the use of your copyright Compositions and the listening/use of Recordings.


The Outlet column shows the online service on which the use of your repertoire was recorded, and the Quantity column shows the number of uses. Please note that the data is also broken down by territories of use.


The report is based on data on actual payments in the reporting period. The period of use of the repertoire on the platform is reflected in the Reporting period begins / ends graphs in the Compositions and Recordings tabs.

The report may also contain information on the applicable royalty rates and deductions made, as well as any adjustments or corrections made to the previously reported data.

articles.title: Why is there no collection data for some platforms in the report?
articles.content:
Some inconsistency in the content of the reports is due to the different schedules for making payments and providing reports by the platforms themselves. Each online service has its own specific features and reporting schedule (monthly or quarterly), as well as its own process for processing requests and paying royalties at different times for copyright and related rights.


The report is first and foremost a financial document and is based on data on actual payments made in the quarter from platforms for listening to your repertoire, not on the actual listening facts.


The information in the report reflects the lag from the actual use (listening) of the repertoire and can be sorted by the Outlet (Online service) and Reporting period begins / ends (Period of use of repertoire on online service) columns.

articles.title: Why is there no information about collections for some works in the report?
articles.content:
In your personal Broma 16 account, all works that have been handed over to us for processing are listed. If a work is present in the personal account and the contract for the Composition is still active, a request for copyright payment will be automatically generated. 

There could be two reasons why there is no revenue shown for a particular work:

  1. The Composition has not been used on the storefront.

  2. Incomplete or incorrect metadata for the Composition or Phonogram prevents it from being accurately matched with storefront data.

articles.title: Why aren't all Artists and ISRCs listed in the Compositions/Works tab?
articles.content:
Unfortunately, it is not always possible to accurately identify the Artist and ISRC for all Compositions. A common issue with collecting copyright fees is the lack of a connection between the musical Composition and the audio recording (phonogram) with the specific Artist and ISRC code. 

This can be due to the way the Composition is used on platforms such as YouTube, where a user may create a cover version of a work and the platform does not provide information about the artist or ISRC. 

To better process reports, we recommend using catalog numbers for Compositions or filtering by the Authors column rather than the Artists column. 

If you have any further questions or need more information, please don't hesitate to reach out to us and we will be happy to assist you.

articles.title: The report includes a small amount of compensation. How can I receive my payout?
articles.content: We only make payouts if the amount of compensation in the report (or the total amount of compensation in several past reports) exceeds the minimum threshold agreed upon in the contract. Paying out small amounts is not practical for either party due to the high fees and commissions charged by banks. If the amount of compensation in the report does not meet the minimum threshold, it will be carried over to the next report and added to any additional compensation earned until the minimum threshold is reached and a payout can be made.

articles.title: What is LyricFind?
articles.content:
LyricFind is a global leader in the field of song lyrics. They provide the world's largest and most accurate catalog of lyrics, which includes over 15 million songs from 1.5 million artists in 100+ languages.


Thanks to LyricFind, music services, applications, and websites can safely and legally provide their users with access to full song lyrics. LyricFind also provides copyright owners with the ability to protect their rights.

LyricFind was founded in 2000 and has since become an indispensable tool for many music companies, including Deezer, Shazam, and many others.


LyricFind is a service for anyone interested in music and song lyrics.

articles.title: How to convert a YouTube channel into an Official Artist Channel?
articles.content:
To convert a channel into an Official Artist Channel and assign it a special symbol (note), it must meet several requirements:

  1. The channel must have more than 1000 subscribers.

  2. The channel must not be empty. There must be a thematic design, music videos or versions of songs with lyrics, or links to official websites and topics, the name of the channel must match the Name / Pseudonym of the artist.

  3. The channel must be dedicated to one group or performer and is managed by the author himself or someone on his behalf;

  4. The channel has at least three music videos uploaded through Broma 16;

  5. The channel complies with the YouTube Community Guidelines, Terms of Use and Copyright.

  6. Participation in the YouTube Partner Program;

If your channel meets these requirements, please submit the corresponding request in the Widget on our website.

The review period depends on the platform and can take from one week to several months, please take this into account. We will definitely inform you of the result of the review.

For more information about Official Artist Channels, see the YouTube Help Introduction to Official Artist Channels - YouTube Help.

articles.title: Do you create playlists (topics) for an artist on YouTube and add video releases?
articles.content:
Topics (channels) with videos for the Artist are automatically created on YouTube. These include video copies of releases sent to YouTube Music, such as static video covers of the release with music, also known as Art Tracks. Initially, all new releases go to the general topic "Various Artists", and then the platform transfers them to the artist's topic/playlist. Unfortunately, we cannot influence this process.

If your channel receives the Official Artist Channel (note) status, it will be merged with the Artist Topic and all Art Tracks will be automatically uploaded to it.

Removing a release from the Content ID system is not possible without also removing it from YouTube Music.

articles.title: Do you upload videos to YouTube?
articles.content:
We don't upload videos of your releases to YouTube, only to the YouTube Music and Content ID system. However, static videos with your recordings as copies of releases on the YouTube Music service are automatically created on the YouTube platform, known as Art Tracks. These are collected in a common playlist (topic) by Artist, also created automatically.

You can also upload your songs (compositions) to your main YouTube channel yourself. We don't add Art Tracks to your channel.

If you want to monetize your YouTube video channel, please create a request in the Broma 16 Widget and send us a link to it. We'll add it to the exclusion list (white list) so that requests don't interfere with monetizing your songs.

articles.title: How to Block and Delete a Video that uses our music? How to send a Strike?
articles.content:
We automatically send requests for monetization translation of videos in our favor for subsequent payment to the rightsholder (that is, you).

At the request of the artist, we do not send strikes, for example, if someone posted a cover version of your song on YouTube.

However, if you want to send a request to delete a video on YouTube due to a copyright infringement, you can fill out the request yourself at the following link: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/2807622.

articles.title: How to add our partner's channel to the YouTube whitelist?
articles.content:
To add a channel to the whitelist, submit the corresponding request in the widget on the Broma 16 website.

Note that our company will not monetize the content on this channel, nor will rewards for works and soundtracks presented on the channel be paid.

articles.title: Что такое Арт Треки (Art Tracks)?
articles.content:
Арт Треки (Art Tracks) - это статические видео-обложки релиза с вашей фонограммой, они автоматически создаются со стороны YouTube, как копии релизов на сервисе YouTube Music, и собираются в общую тему (канал) Артиста, также созданную автоматически.
Арт Треки невозможно перенести на основной YouTube канал, поскольку для этого нужно соответствовать требованиям для получения нотки (OAC). 


Только после присвоения каналу статуса OAC, релизы из Топика появятся в плейлисте основного канала.

articles.title: Что значит “Заявка (Claim)” или страйк?
articles.content:
Заявка (Claim) - позволяет переводить монетизацию музыкального контента, фонограмм и произведений, на который нам были переданы права, в пользу Broma 16, для дальнейшей выплаты вашей стороне. Также просим обратить внимание, что Claim не является Страйком и не несет угрозы вашему каналу.


Если вы хотите заниматься монетизацией контента на своём YouTube канале самостоятельно, пожалуйста, отправьте заявку в виджете “Добавить канал  в WhiteList”, мы добавим канал в список исключений.

Обратите внимание, если на канале YouTube из списка исключений (white list), будет использовано ваше произведение или фонограмма, система Content ID не определит ваш видеоролик для заявки прав, а следовательно мы не сможем его монетизировать.
